dedupe_keys.name: osmre e amlis enhanced abandoned mine land inventory system

description: The national inventory of abandoned coal mine land problems in the United States. The OSMRE page says e-AMLIS holds information on the location, type and extent of abandoned mine land problems left by legacy coal mining, together with the cost of reclaiming them and the reclamation already done, built from field surveys by states, tribes and OSMRE. Problems are grouped into 18 problem types in Priority 1 and 2 (threats to health and safety) plus Priority 3 environmental problems. The inventory is searchable online without charge and questions go to the listed e-AMLIS contact. State layers derive from it: the Pennsylvania Spatial Data Access page for that state's abandoned mine land inventory says it is a subset of the OSMRE inventory. Coverage is the coal-mining states and tribal lands of the United States. Caveats: the page read does not state a licence, a bulk download format or an update date, and non-coal mines are outside its scope. For simulation it gives the location and type of hazards such as open portals, subsidence, dangerous highwalls and polluted water near roads, rail and settlements. A related catalogue record is the USGS USMIN mine features dataset.
